389.s: Challis explains Eastwood Lane's harmonies and how they resembled Bix's use of sixths, ninths and augmented chords.
389.q: Let's see, I think that Eastwood Lane was a guy like Bix. There are several things in there that seem to me he got them from the effect of the Fawn, the orchestral effects. They both loved the orchestra, I'm sure. I didn't know Eastwood, but it's the harmonies that attracted Bix. He used to play --…

389.t: Bix at the piano and notating his compositions
389.s: Challis notated Bix's five piano pieces exactly and describes them as pianistic yet orchestral with a cornet-like melody.
389.q: But Eastwood Lane, I become more familiar with it, but I was made acquainted with it through Beiderbecke, I would say. He used to -- if we would go to a new job, if we got to a job and there was a piano there, or if after the job, there was a piano there and it's nice, he used to liked to sit down…

389.t: Notating In a Mist with Bix and Jack Robbins's added theme
389.s: Publisher Jack Robbins asked him to get Bix's piano piece on paper, which took about six months and ended with Bix improvising an ending and a slow theme.
389.q: But this is the fall of -- I think it's 27. -- No, '28. And we have a guy, Jack Robbins, who was a great publisher, I think, and he was in business with Paul. They had a thing called Whiteman Publications and he was hanging around the band quite a bit and he wanted -- like he got Malnyck and…

389.t: Bix's piano pieces sound alike; transcribing Davenport Blues
389.s: He explains the family resemblance of Bix's pieces and how he wrote Davenport Blues from a record after Bix's death.
389.ch: Bix after Whiteman and his piano pieces
389.q: Yeah, well, this is what -- this is what -- well, I think he could have gotten over it. Now, "Davenport Blues" was done way back.

389.t: For No Reason at All in C and why he refused to notate it
389.s: He declined to transcribe it because it was improvisation on I'd Climb the Highest Mountain with little thematic material.
389.ch: Bix after Whiteman and his piano pieces
389.q: They were trying to get as much material as possible. Now, he used to do one -- he did one that he called For No Reason at All in C." And they gave me that to do too. But if you listen to it, it's just a hodge-podge of improvisation. In other words, there's little or no thematic material that you…

389.t: Notating In a Mist and Candlelights for Jack Robbins
389.s: He recounts getting In a Mist down on paper, adding the broad theme, then Candlelights, flashes and In the Dark in the same formula.
389.ch: Bix after Whiteman and his piano pieces
389.q: Yeah. And he said -- Will you put this down on paper? And he says, 'I'd like to get it.' So we went to work on that, and it was quite a job. At first, it sounded like it might be easy, but even on 'In a Mist' --

389.s: Challis imagines Bix developing his piano works and recording like Harry James or Kaempfert if he had lived.
389.ch: Bix after Whiteman and his piano pieces
389.q: I think, you know, coupled with his playing -- Jesus, the way things were at that time, there was nothing. He couldn't drop anything and go play somewhere; that is, play his trumpet, which was what he was known for. But I think he would have developed his piano things. You know, in my estimation, a…

752.s: Mugsy says Bix was influenced by piano and would perhaps have turned to the classics.
752.q: He was quite a pure player then. He was? He was really influenced by the piano. Yes. Oh, that shows on his records. On his piano things. Did he write most of his tunes on the piano? Oh, yes. Those are all original. To me, on the piano. No one knows what he really amounted to for your life today.…

47.t: Bix at the piano and organ, and Hoagy
47.s: Bix's drive toward piano and composing, playing the pipe organ in Indianapolis, and how Hoagy worked at the piano.
47.q: that was his love the first thing he ever started playing was drums then he picked up the cornet and taught himself how to play cornet he pushed two of those things down and you only push both to push one isn't that right something like that yeah instead of one or something yeah what's the…

753.t: Bix's late piano pieces and a new book on Bix
753.s: Bix wrote piano pieces near the end, transcribed by Bill Challis; Cullum praises a translated French book about Bix.
753.q: The piano pieces, some of those, they came at different times. But the last couple of those came at the end when he was hardly able to play the cornet and he was having so much trouble. And I think that he would sit there and do these things. Bill Challis went over and took them down and I think…
